doesNotAward: Using π × (1.4 × 10^9)^2 is wrong physics; hence no marks in this show question

build.modelAnswer: {1}The microwaves from T are transverse and are already plane polarised.{/1} {2}At 0° and 180° the grille blocks all of the polarised waves, so the signal is zero. At 90° the grille lets all of the microwaves through, so the signal is a maximum.{/2}

indicativeContent.text: At 0° or 180° the grille blocks (all) the (polarised) waves and at 90° the grille allows all the microwaves to pass
Allow E field perpendicular to direction of motion; allow explanation in terms of I = I_0 cos^2 θ

doesNotAward: The grille makes the microwaves polarised (they are polarised before they reach it)

build.modelAnswer: {1}Reflection: the waves bounce off the solid barrier.{/1} {2}Diffraction: the waves spread out as they pass the end of the barrier.{/2}

indicativeContent.text: Allow correct annotation of Fig. 19.1 for each effect

rows.a: 0.45 m (not 0.9 m, which is peak to trough)

modelAnswer: {1}Q is 0.5 m behind P, so the fraction of a wavelength is 0.5 ÷ 4 = 1/8{/1}

indicativeContent.text: Allow ECF from (i). Allow one significant figure

doesNotAward: 0.45 ÷ 0.15 = 3 (forgets that intensity depends on amplitude squared)

indicativeContent.text: the maximum displacement from equilibrium or rest position (allow zero or undisturbed for equilibrium)
number of oscillations / vibrations (at a point) per unit time; or number of wavelengths passing a point or produced by the wave source per unit time (allow per second)
how far ‘out of step’ (out of sync) the oscillations at two points on the wave / string are; alt: the fraction of a cycle between the oscillations at the two points

doesNotAward: Phase difference that compares two different waves instead of two points on the same wave

build.modelAnswer:
1. {1}The points P, Q, R and S all oscillate with the same frequency and the same amplitude.{/1}
2. {2}They all have different phases, so each one has a different phase difference from O.{/2}

indicativeContent.text: all have same frequency or same amplitude
all have different phases / phase differences (allow not in phase or all out of phase)

doesNotAward: Withhold mark if extra incorrect answers given
Treating it as a stationary wave (a progressive wave has no points of zero amplitude)

rows.q: Q14 Angle to the normal of the ray leaving the glass
rows.a: B   15°. Angle of incidence = 10°, n of glass = 1.5: 1.0 × sin r = 1.5 × sin 10°, so r = 15°.

indicativeContent.text: t = [6.0 − 5.0] × 10^-15 = 1.0 × 10^-15 (s) (A0: show question). Allow other correct methods

doesNotAward: Omitting or incorrect use of 1.2 is XP

indicativeContent.text: Allow 1 SF of 2 × 10^-15. Allow 1 mark for 2.4 × 10^-15 (s); 2.5 × 10^8 m s^-1 used

rows.q: Q15(iii) Phase difference between the rays at Y
Q16(a) Speed of red light in glass and in oil
rows.a: glass: 1.97 × 10^8 m s^-1, oil: 2.05 × 10^8 m s^-1 (in that order)

doesNotAward: Using 45° instead of 90° for the angle of refraction (sin 90° = 1)

build.modelAnswer: The ray meets the lower left face at 45°, which is more than the critical angle of 41°. {1}It is totally internally reflected, turns through 90° and travels horizontally to the lower right face.{/1} {2}At 45° again it is totally internally reflected and travels vertically upwards, parallel to the incident ray, and leaves the block.{/2}

indicativeContent.text: TIR shown at lower left-hand boundary with ray turned through 90° and horizontally to the lower right-hand boundary (by eye)
TIR shown at lower right-hand boundary with ray returning vertically parallel to incident ray (exiting glass block) (by eye)

doesNotAward: Any ray drawn refracting out of the block at the lower faces
Using an angle of 45° or 41° rather than 90°

rows.q: Q16(d)(ii) Path of the ray with oil in the beaker
rows.a: 45° is less than the critical angle of 74°, so the ray leaves the glass into the oil and bends (slightly) away from the normal.

rows.task: Fully explain (in purple pen) the correct answer for each question you got incorrect.
Explain how intensity depends on distance from a point source of EM waves. Explain how to calculate the number of photons when given total power output and photon energy.
Describe how rotating a polarising filter through 180° affects the amount of energy transmitted when plane polarised waves are incident.
Draw a diagram illustrating the key phenomenon being observed.
Define the terms amplitude, wavelength. Describe how to calculate phase difference. Describe how intensity depends on amplitude.
Define the terms amplitude, frequency, phase difference.
Explain how to calculate angle of refraction when given refractive index.
Using the same scenario as in Question 15, answer each subquestion using a refractive index of 1.33 and a wavelength of 5.5x10^-7 m.

Draw a diagram illustrating how the ray of light behaves if the angle of incidence is greater than, equal to and smaller than the critical angle. Describe how to calculate the critical angle when given refractive index.

questions.q: The amplitude of a wave is doubled. How does the intensity of the wave change? A decrease by factor of 4  B decrease by factor of 2  C increase by factor of 2  D increase by factor of 4

A sound wave is incident at the ear. The amplitude of the sound wave is 7.8 nm. The intensity of the sound at the earhole is 4.8 × 10^-7 W m^-2. A different sound wave is now incident at the ear. The intensity of this wave is 9.6 × 10^-7 W m^-2. Calculate the amplitude A in nm of this sound wave.

The intensity of a laser beam is 2.0 W m^-2. The cross-sectional area of the beam is 1.0 mm^2. What is the energy delivered by the laser beam in a time of 100 s? A 2.0 × 10^-6 J  B 2.0 × 10^-4 J  C 2.0 × 10^-1 J  D 2.0 × 10^1 J
This question is about a laser pen. Define the terms phase difference and coherence.
questions.a: phase difference: difference in degrees / radians / angle between points on the same wave or (similar) points on two waves; coherence: constant / fixed phase difference

questions.q: A progressive wave of amplitude a has intensity I. This wave combines with another wave of amplitude 0.6a at a point in space. The phase difference between the waves is 180°. What is the resultant intensity of the combined waves in terms of I? A 0.16 I  B 0.4 I  C 1.6 I  D 2.6 I
Electromagnetic waves can be polarised. Explain what plane polarised wave means.
questions.a: oscillations / vibrations are perpendicular to the direction of propagation / energy transfer; oscillations / vibrations are in one direction / one plane

questions.q: Visible light can be plane polarised. Explain why sound waves cannot be plane polarised.
questions.a: Polarisation is when oscillations are (only) in one direction perpendicular to direction of propagation; sound waves are longitudinal; the oscillation is parallel to the direction of propagation

questions.q: Unpolarised light is observed through a single polarising filter. The intensity of the light transmitted by the filter is half the intensity of the incident light. What happens to the intensity of the transmitted light when the filter is rotated through 90°? A decreases  B decreases and then increases  C increases  D does not change
Light travels from air to water. The refractive index of water is greater than the refractive index of air. Compare the speed, frequency and wavelength of light in air and in water.
questions.a: Speed of light is less in water; frequency is the same (in both); wavelength is smaller in water

questions.q: Light can be refracted. Light can also show total internal reflection. Define refractive index of a material.
questions.a: (refractive index) = speed of light in vacuum ÷ speed of light in material (allow n = c / v if all terms defined)

questions.q: The refractive index of B is 1.3 times greater than the refractive index of A. The angle φ is now varied between 0° and 90° with the light still travelling from material A towards the boundary. Explain whether or not total internal reflection will be observed at the boundary between the two materials.
questions.a: (No total internal reflection) Internal reflection / critical angle can only occur for light travelling from B to A
